FORM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL THE DATE OF PAYMENT.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE T.G. SHIVASHANKARE GOWDA  ORAL JUDGMENT
In this appeal, the APSRTC is questioning the quantum of compensation, rate of interest and also contributory negligence on the part of the deceased Ramamurthy.
2. For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Undisputedly there was an accident on 26.10.20213 at 12.30 p.m., while the deceased was travelling in the APSRTC bearing registration No.AP-29-Z-1629 at Makalidura Cross Bangalore-Hindupur Road, the deceased fell down from the footboard due to sudden application of the break by the driver of the bus.
He sustained head injuries and succumbed to death at the spot.
The petitioner, the mother, approached the Tribunal for a grant of compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-.
The claim was opposed by the APSRTC.
The Tribunal, after taking the evidence and hearing both parties, awarded compensation NC: 2024:KHC:37633 of Rs.12,14,000/- with 9% interest.
Pleading that the Tribunal has erroneously taken 50% of future prospectus, awarded 9% interest and contributory negligence on the part of the deceased was not considered, APSRTC is before this Court.

4. Heard the argument of Sri. D.Vijayakumar, learned counsel for the APSRTC and Sri. Vishwanatha Sabarad, learned counsel for the petitioner.
5.

It is contended by the learned counsel for the APSRTC that the deceased was travelling in the footboard, he has all of a sudden jumped out of the bus for no reason and he has contributed himself to the accident in question.
The Tribunal has erroneously not considered the said aspect.
The deceased was aged 19 years, he was a student and he had no proof of earning.
The Tribunal has allowed 50% of future prospectus and awarded the excess compensation.
The interest at 9% was awarded without any reason, no banks will offer such rate of interest at the relevant point of time and sought for modification.

6. Percontra, learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that the applicable future prospectus is no doubt NC: 2024:KHC:37633 40%, the income taken by the Tribunal is on the lower side, as in the year 2013 a person with no proof of income will earn not been less than Rs.8,000/-.

He has no The Managing Director vs Smt. Renukamma on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97702557/
2 objection for recalculation of the compensation accordingly.

sentences.text: On considering Rs.8,000/- as the notional income of the deceased with 40% future prospectus, 50% deduction towards personal expenses, an applicable multiplier of '18' and conventional heads is added, compensation is on the higher side, rather the Tribunal awarded Rs.12,14,000/-, it is just and proper.
7. The arguments on behalf of the APSRTC that the compensation shall not exceed the claim at Rs.10,00,000/- cannot be sustained as the Tribunal is required to award just compensation.
8. As regards the rate of interest is concerned, the Tribunal awarded 9% interest.
On perusal of the impugned judgment, there is no reasons assigned why an interest of 9% is awarded.
As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the APSRTC, in the year 2013, no Banks will offer interest at 9%.
For the special reasons to be recorded, the interest on the higher side can be awarded.

The Division Bench of this court in Ms.Joyeeta Bose and Ors. -vs- Venkateshan.V. and Ors. in M.F.A.No.5896/2018 c/w M.F.A.Nos.4444/2018 and 4659/2018 (MV) DD 24.08.2020 with reference to Section 149(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Rule 253 of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 and Section 34 of Civil Procedure Code, at Para 52 has laid down principles regarding award of interest, it reads thus:
"52.

Thus, under Section 34 of CPC being squarely applicable to the interest awarded by the tribunal and Section 34 empowering the tribunal to award pendente lite interest and discretion being vested with the Court/Tribunal to award interest from the date of suit or petition is to the maximum extent of 6% p.a. or in other words, not exceeding 6% p.a., the contention raised by the learned Advocates appearing for the Insurance Company deserves to be accepted and accordingly, it is accepted.

. . . . . . . .
. . ."
In the light of above judgment interest at the rate of 9% per annum is not justified and it shall be 6%
per annum.
10. The material on record clearly goes to show that the deceased was travelling above of the footboard.
The bus conductor who was examined as R.W.2 admitted that at the time of accident, the petitioner was not on the footboard steps but he was above the footboard.

There is no evidence why the deceased jumped out of the bus on his own cannot be NC: 2024:KHC:37633 sustained, and for the reason of the sudden application of the break, the deceased was thrown out of the footboard.
If the door was locked with a shutter, there could not have been such an incident.
Hence, the plea of contributory negligence urged on behalf of the bus is not persuasive, complete negligence is on the part of the bus.

11. In view of the discussion above, the appeal merits consideration, in the result, the following:
JUDGMENT The Managing Director vs Smt. Renukamma on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97702557/
3 i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The impugned judgment and award is modified.
iii) The petitioner is entitled to interest at 6% instead of 9% awarded by the Tribunal on the compensation.
iv) The APSRTC shall deposit the entire compensation with interest at the rate of 6%
of per annum from the date of the petition till the date of deposit within eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
